Freeze Thu & Fri mornings, mid 20s in low spots

east_texas.headline: Sleet is mixing in near Dallas. A few pellets could reach us this afternoon, then freezing mornings on Thanksgiving and Friday.
east_texas.summary: A light band of rain is moving east from the Metroplex, and spotters from Fort Worth to Waco to Ennis have reported sleet mixed in this morning, even with temperatures in the mid 40s. The air near the ground is very dry, so falling precipitation cools itself as it evaporates and some of it reaches the ground as sleet or soft ice pellets. If the band holds together it reaches the Tyler area around 3 to 5 PM. Most models weaken it before it gets here, so the chance of any precipitation is low, but a brief burst could include a few pellets. Temperatures stay well above freezing, so there is no ice on roads. Clearing behind it sets up freezing mornings Thursday and Friday.
east_texas.rain_note: About a 20% chance of light rain from mid afternoon into tonight. About a 10 to 15% chance of seeing a few sleet or graupel pellets mixed in, best west of Tyler and in any heavier burst. Temperatures stay in the 40s, so nothing freezes on the ground. Not enough to help the drought.

panels.title: Why sleet can fall at 45 degrees
paras: This morning's weather balloon at Fort Worth found the air freezing about a mile up, with very dry air below it. Snow falling from that cold layer starts to melt, but evaporation into the dry air cools it back down, so some of it lands as sleet or soft graupel pellets. That is exactly what spotters reported from Fort Worth to Ennis.

The Shreveport balloon was warmer and moister aloft this morning, but cooler air moves in this evening as the disturbance passes. The best odds of a few pellets are west of Tyler and during any heavier burst. Precipitation will be light and brief, and ground temperatures stay in the 40s, so there is no travel impact.

panels.title: Two cold mornings, then a warm weekend
paras: NWS Shreveport says a quick upper-level disturbance passes tonight with clouds and a slight chance of light rain, mainly south and east of Tyler. Behind it, lows fall near or below freezing Thursday and Friday mornings, from the mid 20s to mid 30s across the region.

Thanksgiving Day looks sunny with highs in the mid 50s. Highs return to the upper 60s and low 70s this weekend, with a small chance of showers Saturday night into Sunday. NWS notes the drought continues with no meaningful rain in sight.

panels.title: Warmer than normal into early December
paras: The Climate Prediction Center favors above-normal temperatures and above-normal precipitation for Texas from Nov 29 to Dec 7, with about average confidence. Most European and GFS ensemble members show at least half an inch of rain for the area sometime Dec 1–8, so the first real rain chance in a while may come early next week.
El Niño remains strong to very strong. It tends to favor an active southern storm track this winter, though NWS Fort Worth notes a strongly negative Pacific pattern may keep it drier than usual.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NWS Fort Worth, mPING spotter reports, NWS weather balloon soundings (Fort Worth and Shreveport), NOAA Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, PowerOutage.us, Weather Underground, Open-Meteo model data (HRRR, GFS, ECMWF, ICON, Canadian, NBM).

tables.note: In town means Tyler, Lindale and other built-up areas. Low spots means rural valleys, creek and river bottoms and sandy open fields, which can run 5 to 9 degrees colder on calm, clear nights. Cover tender plants and bring pets in Wednesday and Thursday nights. Models range from 28 to 37 for Friday morning; on calm, dry nights the colder end usually wins.

hero.label: New snow at high|SNOTEL sites Monday

nm.headline: Monday's snow was light. Icy spots linger on mountain roads this morning before a dry, calm stretch.
nm.summary: Monday's storm left about an inch of new snow at the high SNOTEL sites. Personal weather stations showed the mid teens in the coldest high valleys to near 30 around Taos and Española at sunrise. NWS Albuquerque warns of slick spots on northern mountain roads and patchy fog early this morning. Dry, tranquil weather holds through Thanksgiving, with winds picking up this weekend.

nm.snow_note: Start-of-day readings for Tuesday, after Monday's snow. Each high site gained about an inch. Palo's depth sensor did not report today, so its depth is Monday's. OnTheSnow puts statewide snowpack at 121% of normal.
nm.ski_note: Red River is projected to open Wednesday, and Taos and Ski Santa Fe on Thanksgiving. Sipapu's snow totals were last updated Monday morning. Resort base depths include man-made snow. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Dry and calm, with very cold valley nights
paras: High pressure builds today and Wednesday, keeping winds light and skies mostly clear. NWS has Angel Fire near 10 tonight and in the low teens Wednesday night, with Red River around 18 to 22.
Thanksgiving looks dry with some high clouds as a weak low passes well to the south.

panels.title: Icy spots this morning
paras: NMRoads lists US-64 between Taos and Eagle Nest and NM-475 to Ski Santa Fe as snow packed and icy. I-25 near Raton Pass, Wagon Mound, Las Vegas and Rowe, and I-40 around Santa Rosa and Tijeras, have wet roads with icy spots. No closures are listed on the interstates.
Fire weather stays below critical levels. NWS notes stronger gusts this weekend as late-fall grasses keep drying.

panels.title: Windier weekend, then watching December
paras: NWS Albuquerque expects breezy to windy days from Friday into early next week, with little or no precipitation and highs 5 to 10 degrees above normal.

The Climate Prediction Center leans above normal for both temperature and precipitation in New Mexico from Nov 29 to Dec 7, with about average confidence. The systems NWS can see so far look mostly dry.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, OnTheSnow, Sipapu snow report, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, Weather Underground.
